41005.name: Clackamas County
41005.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Clackamas County has three ambulance service areas under its 2024 county code: American Medical Response (most of the county), Canby Fire District (Canby area) and Molalla Fire District (Molalla area). Not yet confirmed: whether Lake Oswego Fire Department carries patients in Lake Oswego, and which agency serves the edge areas the county plan routes to Woodburn Ambulance Service.

41011.name: Coos County
41011.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Coos County has six ambulance service areas held by five services: Bay Cities Ambulance (Coos Bay and North Bend areas), Coquille Valley Ambulance, Myrtle Point Ambulance, Powers Ambulance, and Lower Umpqua Hospital EMS (northern Coos County). Bay Cities Ambulance and Lower Umpqua Hospital EMS are seen by their own websites; the Coquille, Myrtle Point and Powers services are not yet confirmed by a recent source.

41013.name: Crook County
41013.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Crook County has three ambulance service areas covering the whole county: Crook County Fire & Rescue (about 88%, including Prineville), Redmond Fire & Rescue (about 2.5%, Powell Butte area) and Bend Fire & Rescue (about 9%, the southwest corner). Rager Emergency Services responds first but does not transport. Alfalfa Fire District, whose boundaries reach into southwest Crook County, began its own ambulance transports in October 2025, and whether it carries patients from the Crook County part of its district is not yet confirmed.

41017.name: Deschutes County
41017.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Deschutes County assigns emergency ambulance service by area (county code 8.30, terms through June 30, 2028). Seen on a public page: Bend Fire & Rescue, Redmond Fire & Rescue, Sisters-Camp Sherman, La Pine, Sunriver, Black Butte Ranch and Crooked River Ranch fire agencies, plus Alfalfa Fire District, which began its own ambulance transports in 2025 under an agreement with Bend Fire. Not yet confirmed: the small far-eastern corner of the county (near Hampton) that the county map assigns to the Burns ambulance area in Harney County.

41021.name: Gilliam County
41021.via: county ASA plans, county GIS ASA layers and agency websites (local sources)
41021.note: Gilliam County has two ambulance service areas: North Gilliam Medic (Arlington and the north of the county) and South Gilliam County Ambulance Service (Condon and the south), meeting near milepost 20 on Highway 19.
a: North Gilliam Medic (North Gilliam County Health District)
South Gilliam County Ambulance Service (South Gilliam County Health District)

41027.name: Hood River County
41027.via: county ASA plans, county GIS ASA layers and agency websites (local sources)
41027.note: Hood River County has three ambulance service areas: Hood River Fire & EMS (Hood River and surroundings), Parkdale Fire District (upper valley) and Cascade Locks Fire & EMS (Cascade Locks).

41029.name: Jackson County
41029.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Jackson County has three ambulance service areas: Mercy Flights (Medford and most of the county), Ashland Fire & Rescue (Ashland and Talent) and Rogue River Fire District (Rogue River and Gold Hill area). Tri-County Ambulance Service, Inc. of Ashland, registered with the state in August 2025, also holds a state ambulance transport licence, and what service it provides in Jackson County is not yet confirmed.

41037.name: Lake County
a: Silver Lake EMS Volunteer Ambulance Unit
North Lake County EMS Volunteer Ambulance Unit

41043.name: Linn County
41043.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Linn County's ambulance service area map (August 2026) names areas for Albany, Lebanon, Sweet Home, Santiam, Lyons, Jefferson, Idanha/Detroit, Corvallis, Sisters, Eugene and Springfield. Which of these reach into Linn County and the service running each are not yet confirmed by a recent source.
a: Black Butte Ranch Rural Fire Protection District

41047.name: Marion County
41047.via: county ASA plans, county GIS ASA layers and agency websites (local sources)
41047.note: Marion County has ten ambulance service areas, each held under a county franchise running January 2024 to December 2029: Salem Fire Department (Salem area; it has run these ambulances itself since July 2025), Keizer Fire District, St. Paul Fire District, Marion County Fire District #1, Woodburn Ambulance Service, Lyons Fire District (the North Santiam canyon), Santiam Hospital ambulance (Stayton area; the hospital joined Salem Health in September 2026), Turner Fire District, Jefferson Fire District and Polk County Fire District #1 (a small area along the Willamette River south of Salem).
a: St. Paul Rural Fire Protection District

41051.name: Multnomah County
41051.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. American Medical Response holds Multnomah County's single 911 ambulance contract, which runs through August 31, 2028. Not yet confirmed: whether neighbouring agencies that answer calls at the county's edges under agreements, such as Cascade Locks Fire & EMS in the eastern Columbia River Gorge and the area along Highway 30 next to Columbia County, also carry patients from those areas.

41053.name: Polk County
a: Southwestern Polk County Rural Fire Protection District

41059.name: Umatilla County
41059.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. Umatilla County has six ambulance service areas (county map, June 2026): Pendleton, Hermiston/Umatilla, Milton-Freewater, Mill Creek (served from Walla Walla), Athena/Weston, and the Confederated Tribes of the Umatilla Indian Reservation. The service running each area is not yet confirmed by a recent source.

41067.name: Washington County
41067.note: Unverified lead, not yet independently checked. American Medical Response (AMR) holds Washington County's emergency ambulance franchise for the county's single ambulance service area; the fire departments respond first but do not hold it. The Washington County parts of Wilsonville, Lake Oswego and Rivergrove are served from Clackamas County, and the area south of Bell Road and Highway 99W is in Tualatin Valley Fire & Rescue's Yamhill County service area; who transports in those small areas is not yet confirmed.
